To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
feeding All-G Rich to heifers increased PUFA content of beef but had undesirable effects on beef color and palability.
feeding microalgae to heifers increased the PUFA content and decreased the flavor and color stability of 85/ 15 ground beef.
feeding microalgae (All-G Rich) meal to finishing heifers increases ground beef polyunsaturated fatty acid content, but also negatively affects beef flavor and color stability.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of feeding a natural source of omega-3 fatty acids to beef cattle and how this affects the fatty acid composition, sensory palatability, color stability, and consumer acceptance of 85/85 ground beef patties.
the effects of feeding algae meal to finishing heifers, and the effects of feeding the algae meal to heifers on ground beef color, palatability and fatty acid profile.
the use of microalgae as a source of n-3 PUFA in the beef industry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
feeding microalgae to heifers is not recommended for improving the fatty acid content of 85:15 ground beef.
feeding 150 g·d of microalgal meal to beef heifers does not improve ground beef palatability and color stability.
the use of microalgae to improve the PUFA profile of ground beef is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
feeding microalgae to finishing heifers increases the n-3 PUFA content of beef but has a negative impact on beef flavor and color stability.
microalgae meal is not recommended for feeding to finishing heifers.
microalgae meal should not be fed to finishing heifers at the levels evaluated in our study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
increasing dietary microalgae concentration increases the PUFA in ground beef and decreases the shelf life of the product.
the use of microalgae as an alternative to traditional lipid supplements should be evaluated on a case by case basis.
the use of microalgae as an alternative feed ingredient to increase the n-3 fatty acid content of ground beef should be approached with caution.
